clue.text: No holds barred in casual approach to fielding?

definitions.meaning: a free style of wrestling in which any hold is allowed
read literally, a fielder grabbing at the ball any way they can

explanation.walkthrough: Fielding is the cricket job of stopping and catching the ball, so the second reading is a fielder grabbing whatever comes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an all-in wrestling style and, more loosely, any method with no rules at all.

clue.text: Scenes for 26: (2) crooked deal by assistant …

indicators.note: something crooked is bent out of true, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: A dodgy deal struck with a helper, introducing a series of venues for the Ashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' turns DEAL into ADEL. The bracketed numbers give the order of the five Test matches of the 2010-11 Ashes series in Australia; 2-down's definition covers the run of ellipsis clues.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian city hosted the second Test of an Ashes series, so it is one of the scenes of that contest.

clue.text: … (3) forward on horse …

parts.note: forward in the sense of cheeky or impudent means pert
H is slang shorthand for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A bold rider pushing ahead on a mount.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bracketed (3), continuing 2-down's 'Scenes for 26': the third Test of the Ashes series. Horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: This Western Australian city staged the third Test match in the series of Australian venues listed.

clue.text: … (1) rise of salts in salt …

indicators.note: the reversed sailors go inside the salty water

parts.note: brine is salt water

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads from bottom to top, so the word is turned around

parts.note: salts are old sailors, as are ABs (able seamen)

explanation.surface: Salt crystals forming as brine evaporates.
explanation.walkthrough: Salts are old sailors; 'rise of' reads them upward in this down clue. The (1) marks the first Test of the Ashes series, picking up 2-down's definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queensland capital hosted the first Test match in the list of Australian venues.

clue.text: … (5) poet and soldier …

definitions.meaning: the fifth Test venue in the Ashes series of 2-down
Sir Philip Sidney, Elizabethan poet who died fighting at Zutphen, whose name was often spelt with a y in his own era

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Philip Sidney is usually spelt with an i today, but older texts spell him with a y, and the city was named for a Sydney.
explanation.definitionFit: The New South Wales capital hosted the fifth Test, and shares its name with the Elizabethan soldier-poet.

clue.text: … (4) river not ending in mountains

indicators.note: the shortened river sits inside the mountain range

parts.note: the Mountains of Mourne are a range in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: the river's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the Elbe is a river of central Europe

explanation.surface: A river that runs out among the peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ending' cuts ELBE to ELB, which goes into MOURNE. The (4) is the fourth Test venue, continuing 2-down's definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian capital hosted the fourth Test match of the Ashes series in the list.

clue.text: Call to puke regrettably after state of 3

indicators.note: the anagram follows the state abbreviation

parts.note: WA is Western Australia, the state whose capital is Perth (3-down)

indicators.note: a regrettable outcome is one gone wrong, so these letters go wrong into a new order

explanation.surface: A rude morning summons for someone who was sick in Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regrettably' rearranges PUKE into KEUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A morning summons to rouse a sleeper, as in a hotel's early telephone call.

clue.text: Fish turned to bull in Spain when Keith, correspondent of the Queen, gets appropriate degree

indicators.note: the fish's name is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a cod is a fish
toro is Spanish for bull
Keith Flett is famous for his many published letters to newspapers
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina, and 'of' makes it possessive ER's

explanation.surface: A rambling tale of a fish, a Spanish bull and a prolific letter writer winning a fitting honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes COD into DOC. The degree is apt because Keith Flett is the archetypal letter writer to the Guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: A higher degree in literature or the humanities, fitting for someone so devoted to writing letters.

clue.text: See 22
Inspirer of poetry by lecturer at Oxford

indicators.note: the name lies right by, straddling, the boundary of these words

explanation.surface: A muse attributed to an Oxford don.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'lecturER AT Oxford'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is the muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Firm on fire is causing bellyache

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
something on fire is lit

explanation.surface: A company whose premises are burning gives someone a stomach ache.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the colon causes abdominal pain, here called a bellyache.

clue.text: Brutus, it was said, made good return in case

indicators.note: the word for good comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: bon is French for good
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: Brutus repaid a kindness, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Antony in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar calls Brutus 'the noblest Roman of them all'. 'return' turns BON into NOB; 'made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare has Brutus described as the most honourable Roman, so the superlative is what was said of him.

clue.text: A team's centre of revolution

parts.note: a football or cricket team is an eleven, XI, with the 's kept as S

explanation.surface: One side's player who acts as the pivot of the team.
explanation.definitionFit: The line about which a body rotates is its pivotal centre of turning.

clue.text: Wee woolly with springy harness

definitions.meaning: a small knitted sweater for an infant
a seat on springs or elastic hung from a doorway for an infant to bounce in

explanation.walkthrough: A woolly is a knitted sweater; the bouncing seat is known in Britain by a brand-like name for an infant's bouncer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a little knitted pullover and an infant's bouncing harness.

clue.text: Religious life is belief in royalty without the royal

indicators.note: the royal letter is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: monarchism is support for rule by a king or queen
R stands for Rex or Regina, the royal abbreviation

explanation.surface: Faith in the Crown with no one on the throne becomes a calling.
explanation.definitionFit: The monastic system, a life of vows lived apart for faith, is a religious way of life.

clue.text: Runner to behold setter in body cavity

parts.note: Sebastian Coe is a British Olympic middle-distance runner
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
the setter of the crossword refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: An athlete watches a crossword compiler inside an anatomy diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe was a British Olympic champion at 1500 metres.
explanation.definitionFit: A coelome, more often coelom, is the main fluid-filled cavity within an animal's body.

clue.text: Wizard with standard return outside

indicators.note: the reversed banner surrounds the joining word
the banner comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a standard is a flag
and means with, together with

explanation.surface: A sorcerer carrying a banner back outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link but supplies letters; 'return' reads the banner backwards before it wraps them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's grey wizard of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings is a famous magician.

clue.text: Lack of detectives probing horse is disastrous to race

indicators.note: the missing police go into the horse as a probe enters

parts.note: gee or gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
no CID: the CID is the British police's Criminal Investigation Department

explanation.surface: Missing police inspect a racehorse, which proves disastrous at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as wordplay 'is' definition: the crime is what is disastrous to a race of people. The CID is the detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate killing of a whole people is the thing most catastrophic to an ethnic group.

clue.text: Promptness, city style, arresting redhead

indicators.note: the city phrase holds the letter captive inside it

parts.note: a la city, in the manner of the city
the head of red is R

explanation.surface: Quick work by city police in detaining a red-haired suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity is eager readiness, a brisk willingness to act at once.

clue.text: Alfresco eateries are a bore, regressing into adolescence

indicators.note: the turned phrase goes inside the adolescent years

parts.note: the teens are the years of adolescence

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word for bore reads in reverse

parts.note: a drag is a bore, something tedious

explanation.surface: Teenagers find outdoor cafes tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressing' turns DRAG to GARD; A plus GARD goes into TEENS; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardens where tea is served outdoors are open-air places to eat and drink.

clue.text: Bisyllabic hooligan meets trisyllabic American

definitions.meaning: a Parisian street ruffian, said in French in two syllables
a member of a Native American people of the south-west, said in English in three syllables

explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling names a Paris street thug (French, two syllables) and a Native American people (three).

clue.text: Scientist additional to 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6?

definitions.meaning: Charles ..., the naturalist behind the theory of evolution
another Australian city beyond the five Test venues

explanation.definitionFit: The naturalist of evolution shares his name with the capital of Australia's Northern Territory, a city like the others.

clue.text: Fit as a fiddle though heat had nearly killed me

indicators.note: the fodder is struck down, wrecked and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Someone in perfect health despite nearly dying in the heatwave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killed me' rearranges all thirteen letters of 'heat had nearly'; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means robust and in excellent health, just as the simile about the fiddle does.

clue.text: Girl coming under the foregoing?

definitions.meaning: ... Springs lies far south of, under, Darwin, the previous clue

explanation.walkthrough: Alice Springs is a town in the middle of Australia, on the road south from Darwin (21-down).
explanation.definitionFit: A common girl's name that also begins the Australian town lying south of the preceding city.

clue.text: Plant and lay out from varied 22 9

indicators.note: the letters of the long phrase are varied into new order once some are taken away

parts.note: the answer to 22 and 9 across, the phrase meaning in robust health

explanation.surface: A gardener told to plant and lay out a bed, varied from a healthy scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of the 22/9 phrase, set aside those of AND LAY ('out from'), and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather is a low moorland shrub, a common plant of heaths.

clue.text: Religion about half priced? It's my fault

indicators.note: the sect goes around the shortened word

parts.note: a cult is a religion, especially a fringe one

indicators.note: only the first half of the six-letter word is used

explanation.surface: A sect cutting its prices by half, and someone owning up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is what the guilty party says on owning up, not a description of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The one to blame is the person who would confess that the wrong is theirs.

clue.text: Like men we won

parts.note: as means like
hes are males, men

explanation.surface: An English cricket fan's boast about the team's triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the Test cricket series between England and Australia; England won it in Australia in 2010-11.
explanation.definitionFit: From an English point of view the trophy for the England-Australia Test series was the prize just won.

clue.text: Home Christian keeping pet as a sign

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the designer holds the animal inside his name

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer
a cat is a pet

explanation.surface: A Christian household keeps a pet as an omen.
explanation.definitionFit: An indicator is a sign or pointer showing a state or trend.
